topic: The Wallis Product: An Infinite Dance Toward Pi
target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of Sine Powers
lecture_lines: We start with the integral of sine power.
This area flattens as n increases.
Visualizing sine powers as shrinking curves.
animations: Define integral I_n as sin^n(x) from 0 to pi/2. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg]
Show reduction formula relating I_n to I_{n-2}.
Display recurrence relation clearly for n >= 2.
Highlight base cases I_0 = pi/2 and I_1 = 1.
Summarize the values for even and odd n. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg]

sections.title: Deriving the Ratio: The Key Insight
lecture_lines: Consider the ratio of consecutive integrals.
As n grows, this ratio nears one.
The gap between curves eventually vanishes.
animations: Show the ratio of integral I_n / I_{n+1} using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg].
Demonstrate that this ratio approaches 1 as n increases.
Connect the ratio limit to the Wallis product formula using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microscope.svg].

sections.title: The Wallis Product Formula
lecture_lines: The Wallis product formula emerges here.
Fractions multiply towards pi over two.
Output values converge to pi halves.
Infinite steps reveal the target value.
animations: Assemble the product terms from I_n ratios [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg].
Show the limit as n goes to infinity.
Finalize the Wallis product expression for pi/2 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg].

sections.title: Intuition: Why Pi?
lecture_lines: Why does this involve only integers?
Infinite products connect to transcendental pi.
Each fraction steps along the circle.
animations: Relate trigonometric integrals to circular geometry properties. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg]
Explain why pi emerges from these specific integrals. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/protractor.svg]
Show the connection to the area of a circle. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg]

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Significance
lecture_lines: Pi builds from infinite fractional layers.
animations: Recap the main Wallis product formula components using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg].
Discuss its role in probability and statistics.
End with the profound connection to pi by showing the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coin.svg].
